location.about: Surrounded by trees, grass and spring fed ponds, the center provides a supportive atmosphere where one can learn the practice of Vipassana meditation. This technique, discovered by Buddha twenty-five centuries ago, uses the breath and one's own body as the basis for developing concentration and insight. The courses provide a unique opportunity to direct one's attention inward, and set about a process of inner discovery through direct experience.
location.instructions:
Students may apply to sit for up to two courses at this center if both courses have waiting lists.  Once an application is enrolled, the other application will be canceled.  Students with applications to sit at other centers will be asked to choose which center they want to attend. 
 
COVID Information - Please read before applying.
The health-safety protocol for the Meditation Center in Pecatonica, IL is as follows: 
  • No Covid vaccination required 
  • No masking required  
  • No antigen or PCR test required  
  • Rideshare and public transportation allowed​

Illness While At The Center:  Unfortunately, we do not have the resources to accommodate course participants who arrive or become ill while at the Center.  Participants with signs and symptoms of Covid-19 or other influenza-like symptoms (including stomach flu) will be asked to leave as soon as possible.  Anyone who is unable to independently go home or to a safe destination, will need to ask their emergency contact for assistance. Please make arrangements for this possibility prior to the course.

 

Although the Center is taking precautions, there still remains the risk of exposure to COVID-19 or other contagious illness while at the Center. If you are at risk of serious illness from such exposures, it is advised that you not place yourself at risk by coming to the Center.

Rideshare: Ride offers are on a volunteer basis and there is no guarantee that a ride will be available from your area. Alternate means of transportation should be considered well in advance. If you need a ride or if you're willing to give a ride to another student, we have course-specific Rideshare board. You will find the link to the Rideshare board for your course in the acceptance letter under the Directions and Transportation section.

If you have any questions, please contact us at: registration@pakasa.dhamma.org

location.about: The Southeast Vipassana Center is located in southeastern Georgia in Wayne County, ten miles south of the small town of Jesup, Georgia. It is approximately 70 miles southwest of Savannah, Georgia, 90 miles north of Jacksonville, Florida, and 250 miles southeast from Atlanta, Georgia. Set in a secluded rural area and surrounded by forty acres of beautiful pine, oak, and mixed hardwood forests, the Center provides an ideal meditation environment for Vipassana students in the Southeast.
location.instructions:
✅IMPORTANT:  Please Review These Guidelines Before Applying! 

👉Course Registration
Registration opens at 6 AM Eastern Time on the listed dates. You may apply for up to two courses at this center if both have waitlists. Once enrolled in one course, the other application will be canceled. If you have applications at multiple centers, you will need to choose one.
 
✉️ Checking Emails
We send important communications via email and text. Please check your Spam/Junk folder regularly and respond promptly.  We also recommend adding our email address to your contacts to prevent messages from being filtered out.
 
🚑 Illness at the Center 
If you become ill, you will be required to leave as soon as possible. The center does not have facilities for those who fall ill. Please make sure your emergency contact is prepared to assist.
 
🦠COVID-19 Protocol
No vaccination, masking, or testing is required. Although the center is taking precautions, there remains a risk of COVID-19 exposure. If you are at high risk, please consider this before applying.
 
🚗 Travel Arrangements 
You are responsible for arranging your own travel. The center is not liable for any travel expenses.
 

❓If you have any questions, please contact us at registration@patapa.dhamma.org

location.about: Dhamma Pasava, also known as the Intermountain Vipassana Meditation Center, means "Spring of Dhamma" in Pali. Established in 2016, the center sits on 256 acres of land just 2 minutes from the small resort town of Lava Hot Springs, Idaho and 30 minutes from Pocatello, Idaho. The center is centrally located in the Intermountain Region, less than 2 hours from Salt Lake City. Currently, the center offers approximately 16 ten-day courses every year. In addition, old student courses, including one long-course, Satipatthana courses, 3-day and 1-day courses and work periods are held throughout the year. The center is still in its developing stages, but at full build-out will be able to accommodate 120 students year-round.
location.instructions:
BEFORE YOU APPLY

We ask that applicants apply to only one course at this Center at a time. Although the Center is taking all precautions, there still remains the risk of exposure to COVID-19 while at the Center. If you are at risk of serious illness from Coronavirus, it is advised that you not place yourself at risk by coming to the Center.

**Priority will be given to students from the Intermountain region; applicants who are traveling from outside the region, and will be using public transportation, will need to have an emergency contact in the area or a plan of how you will leave from the Center if you get sick and need to leave the course early**

 
Once you have submitted your application, be sure to check your SPAM folder for communications from pasava.dhamma.org or you may miss important email communications.
 

 


Click the 'Apply' link to complete an application. 

Link available starting 6:00 am MDT on the listed application date. 

Students are expected at the center between 2 and 5 pm for the registration period. The course ends the morning of the last day by 7:00 am.

Once you have completed a course, you can access: 

  • Old Student Regional Site: Welcome Old Students! | Intermountian Vipassana Center

  • Weekly group sittings are also offered for old students. Email us for more info.

location.about: The Shelburne center, founded in 1982, was the first center in North America. The original facility was merely a roomy, comfortable two-story house and barn on eight acres of meadowland. In 1989, a group of meditators donated an adjoining seventy acres of land. Today the center consists of 108 acres and many new buildings have been added, including a two dining rooms, a meditation hall for 200, a 140 cell pagoda, separate residences for men and women and a teacher's residence.
